title: Actogram visualisation
text: examples use ActTrust validation recording bundled zeitR, run run_pipeline_native().
code: FILE <- system.file("extdata", "input1.txt", package = "zeitR") TZ   <- "America/Sao_Paulo"  result <- run_pipeline_native(FILE, tz = TZ, quiet = TRUE) #> ℹ Reading input1.txt ... #> ✔ [input1] Done. 52 main night(s), 0 secondary episode(s).

title: Actogram visualisation
text: plot_actogram() draws one row per calendar day time day (00:00 24:00) x-axis. oldest day top, following standard chronobiology convention. Rows labelled every seven days default.  dark purple band running centre row main sleep period. amber gaps naps; terracotta blocks -wrist episodes.
code: plot_actogram(result, tz = TZ)

title: Actogram visualisation
text: plot_actogram_double() uses classic double-plot format chronobiology: recording day appears twice – left column row (x = 00:00 24:00) right column row (x = 24:00 48:00). dashed vertical line marks 24 h boundary. sleep band drifts diagonally across rows, drift reflects day--day changes circadian phase. stable schedule appears straight vertical band; free-running rhythm traces slanted line.
code: plot_actogram_double(result, tz = TZ)

title: Actogram visualisation
text: plot_actogram_activity() keeps double-plot layout replaces filled tiles vertical bars. bar’s height proportional raw ZCMn activity count; bars coloured sleep/wake state. lets read intensity activity state classification single plot. Bar heights capped 99th percentile non-zero epochs default (activity_cap_quantile = 0.99), handful outlier bursts compress rest range. Zero-activity epochs (sleep, -wrist) receive thin 2% baseline stub remain faintly visible rather disappearing entirely.
code: plot_actogram_activity(result, tz = TZ)

title: Actogram visualisation
text: actogram_colours() returns named hex vector used default palette across three functions. Printing quickest way see current defaults overriding .
code: actogram_colours() #>      wake     sleep       nap off-wrist  #> "#C25E2A" "#3B2F6B" "#F0A500" "#D9C8A0"

title: Actogram visualisation
text: Pass named character vector colours argument. need supply states want change; unnamed states keep default.
code: my_cols <- actogram_colours() my_cols["sleep"]     <- "#1C1A2E"   # darker midnight my_cols["off-wrist"] <- "#8B4513"   # saddle brown  plot_actogram(result, tz = TZ, colours = my_cols)

title: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis
text: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis (NPCRA) characterises 24-hour rest-activity pattern without assuming sinusoidal waveform. introduced Van Someren et al. (1997, 1999) become standard approach actigraphy-based circadian assessment healthy clinical populations. zeitR implements compute_npcra(), returns five core variables single function call.

title: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis
text: quantifies consistent 24-hour activity pattern across days. computed ratio variance average hourly activity profile overall variance raw signal: =np⋅∑h=1p(x‾h−x‾)2∑=1n(xi−x‾)2 \text{} = \frac{n}{p} \cdot \frac{\sum_{h=1}^{p} \left( \bar{x}_h - \bar{x} \right)^2}      {\sum_{=1}^{n} \left( x_i   - \bar{x} \right)^2} nn total number epochs, pp number epochs per day, x‾h\bar{x}_h mean activity hour--day hh, x‾\bar{x} grand mean. Range: 0–1. Higher values indicate stable, clock-driven rhythm. Typical values healthy adults 0.6–0.8.

title: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis
text: IV measures fragmentation rest-activity rhythm — often abruptly signal transitions rest activity: IV=n∑=2n(xi−xi−1)2(n−1)∑=1n(xi−x‾)2 \text{IV} = \frac{n \sum_{=2}^{n} (x_i - x_{-1})^2}                  {(n-1) \sum_{=1}^{n} (x_i - \bar{x})^2} Range: ≥0\geq 0. Higher values indicate fragmented rhythm. Values 1.0 often seen older adults patients neurological disorders.

title: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis
text: RA captures contrast active least active periods day: RA=M10−L5M10+L5 \text{RA} = \frac{M10 - L5}{M10 + L5} Range: 0–1. Higher values indicate stronger amplitude circadian rhythm.

title: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis
text: L5 mean activity level least active 5-hour window 24-hour averaged profile. M10 mean activity active 10-hour window. computed 24-hour average profile (raw epochs), making robust day--day variability. onset times (L5_onset, M10_onset) give start time respective windows HH:MM format.

title: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis
text: compute_npcra() accepts either zeitr_recording (read_actigraphy()) data frame datetime activity columns.
code: rec   <- read_actigraphy("recordings/P001.txt", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo") npcra <- compute_npcra(rec) npcra ## # A tibble: 1 x 10 ##   participant_id    IS    IV    RA    L5 L5_onset   M10 M10_onset n_days n_epochs ##   <chr>          <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>    <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>    <int> ## 1 P001            0.72  0.43  0.89  12.3 02:30    84.7  11:00       7.0     10080

title: Non-parametric circadian rhythm analysis
text: participant P001: = 0.72 — moderately stable rhythm, consistent healthy adult regular working hours. IV = 0.43 — low fragmentation; rest-activity transitions relatively smooth. RA = 0.89 — strong circadian amplitude; large contrast active rest phases. L5 onset = 02:30 — least active window centred around 02:30, expected typical sleeper. M10 onset = 11:00 — active window peaks mid-morning.

title: Physical activity intensity from ActTrust/GT3X+ counts
text: source study fits sqrt(MET) ~ sqrt(activity_counts) * device_placement via linear model indirect-calorimetry data, reports fitted coefficients (Table 2). zeitR doesn’t re-fit model – can’t, without breath--breath VO2 data – applies published coefficients directly: MET=(β0+β1activity_counts)2\text{MET} = \left(\beta_0 + \beta_1 \sqrt{\text{activity\_counts}}\right)^2 pa_equations() returns table four device x placement combinations source study validated: ACTT Condor Instruments’ ActTrust device (PIM mode); GT3X+ ActiGraph’s GT3X+ (vector magnitude). cut3/cut6/cut9 published count/min cut-points 3, 6, 9 MET thresholds – provided reference; functions classify estimated METs directly rather re-deriving .
code: pa_equations() #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   device placement    b0     b1  cut3  cut6  cut9 #>   <chr>  <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 GT3X+  hip        1.06 0.0199  1132  4853  9468 #> 2 ACTT   hip        1.11 0.0088  5057 23339 46410 #> 3 ACTT   wrist      1.23 0.0081  3761 22368 47203 #> 4 GT3X+  wrist      1.21 0.0127  1698  9503 19787

title: From raw accelerometry to PIM/TAT/ZCM activity counts
text: axis DC offset removed (mrpheus::remove_dc()) – important whichever axis carrying gravity, typically ~1 g – band-pass filtered zero-phase (mrpheus::bandpass_filter()). filter primitives already validated part mrpheus’s YASA-parity PSG pipeline, reused rather reimplemented. vector norm computed per sample filtered axes: sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) – filter first, combine, matching order Batista et al. (2026) describe ActTrust. Samples grouped non-overlapping epochs (epoch_sec * sampling_rate samples ). Per epoch: PIM (sum absolute filtered norm), TAT (seconds tat_threshold), ZCM (sign changes beyond zcm_threshold dead-band, summed across three axes).

title: From raw accelerometry to PIM/TAT/ZCM activity counts
text: ’s bundled raw-accelerometer dataset zeitR (inst/extdata’s ActTrust file already epoch-level, everything read_acttrust() produces) – vignette simulates one: 2 minutes near-still noise, followed 2 minutes clear 1 Hz movement, GT3X+-like 25 Hz. first two (quiet) epochs stay near zero every metric; last two (active) epochs show clear PIM, TAT, ZCM elevation – sinusoid crosses zero roughly twice per second, ~120 crossings/epoch active x-axis expected order magnitude.
code: sr        <- 25   # Hz epoch_sec <- 60 n         <- sr * epoch_sec * 4  # 4 epochs total t         <- seq(0, (n - 1) / sr, by = 1 / sr)  set.seed(42) quiet  <- rnorm(sr * epoch_sec * 2, sd = 0.001) active <- sin(2 * pi * 1 * t[(sr * epoch_sec * 2 + 1):n]) * 0.5  x <- c(quiet, active)               # all simulated movement on the x-axis y <- rep(0, n) z <- rnorm(n, sd = 0.01) + 1         # ~1 g gravity offset, small sensor noise counts <- compute_activity_counts(x, y, z, sampling_rate = sr, epoch_sec = epoch_sec) counts #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   epoch    PIM   TAT   ZCM #>   <int>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1     1   4.91  0        8 #> 2     2   6.65  0.52     6 #> 3     3 477.   57.5    127 #> 4     4 477.   57.6    123 ggplot(counts, aes(x = factor(epoch), y = PIM)) +   geom_col(fill = "#C25E2A") +   labs(x = "Epoch", y = "PIM", title = "PIM per epoch: quiet -> active") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

text: circ_mean_h() circ_sd_h() compute circular statistics clock-time variables. Using standard arithmetic mean times like sleep onset (often straddles midnight) inflates variability estimates produces biased means; circular mean handles wrap correctly. circ_mean_h() function returns decimal hours [0, 24). display HH:MM:

main <- native$nights |> filter(sleep_type == "main")  # Decimal hours of bed time and get-up time onset_h  <- as.numeric(format(main$bed_time,    "%H", tz = TZ)) +             as.numeric(format(main$bed_time,    "%M", tz = TZ)) / 60 offset_h <- as.numeric(format(main$get_up_time, "%H", tz = TZ)) +             as.numeric(format(main$get_up_time, "%M", tz = TZ)) / 60  cat(sprintf("Mean sleep onset:  %05.2f h  (SD = %.2f h)
",             circ_mean_h(onset_h),  circ_sd_h(onset_h))) #> Mean sleep onset:  23.80 h  (SD = 0.89 h) cat(sprintf("Mean sleep offset: %05.2f h  (SD = %.2f h)
",             circ_mean_h(offset_h), circ_sd_h(offset_h))) #> Mean sleep offset: 07.73 h  (SD = 0.77 h) fmt_h <- function(h) sprintf("%02d:%02d", as.integer(h) %% 24L,                               as.integer((h %% 1) * 60))  cat("Mean sleep onset: ", fmt_h(circ_mean_h(onset_h)),  "
") #> Mean sleep onset:  23:47 cat("Mean get-up time: ", fmt_h(circ_mean_h(offset_h)), "
") #> Mean get-up time:  07:43

title: zeitR — Actigraphy parsing and analysis for R
text: zeitR R package importing, parsing, analysing raw actigraphy recordings wrist-worn devices. runs full rest-activity pipeline — -wrist detection, sleep period identification, WASO computation — computes standard non-parametric circadian rhythm variables (, IV, RA, L5, M10), returning tidy data frames ready downstream chronobiological analysis. zeitR ships two end--end pipelines: run_pipeline() — Condor CSPD pipeline, validated epoch--epoch Condor circadiaBase Python reference. run_pipeline_native() — Vallim pipeline, post-processing layer developed Julia Ribeiro da Silva Vallim replaces Condor’s classification logic adaptive 7-rule rule set (Fix 25, 26a/b/c, 27, 29, Rules 3–7). Handles edge cases including fragmented episodes, long sleep periods, date collisions, adaptive nocturnal window inference wrist temperature ambient light. zeitR designed complement slumbR Circadia Lab ecosystem: slumbR handles sleep diary questionnaire data, zeitR handles actigraphy side study. Beyond two pipelines, zeitR also estimates energy expenditure classifies physical activity (PA) intensity raw ActTrust/GT3X+ activity counts, using published equations (see pa_equations() Features ) – extending zeitR beyond sleep half 24 h rest-activity cycle. compute_activity_counts() extends one step back: devices pipelines provide raw triaxial acceleration samples rather onboard-computed counts, converts epoch-level PIM/TAT/ZCM shape read_acttrust() already produces.
